the use of digital libraries in an individual’s daily life.
how people use and manage personal music collections, and how this knowledge can inform the design of personal music digital libraries.

a personal music digital libraries should support the following user behaviors: (1) browsing and searching by genre and mood, (2) browsing and searching for music by artist and title, (3) browsing by album, (4) browsing and searching based on a particular playlist, (5) browsing and searching within a playlist, (6) browsing by year, and (7) browsing by track length.
personal music digital libraries must support a variety of organizational and access techniques.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are interested in the intersection of the fields of digital libraries and information retrieval, as it relates to the personal music collection.

a personal music digital libraries should support the user’s ability to organize music into meaningful categories, to search for music using multiple criteria, to browse the collection, and to listen to music while searching for other music.

a personal music digital libraries needs to support: 1) multiple, overlapping organization techniques, 2) a variety of access methods (e.g., searching, browsing) that support different types of access, and 3) the ability to use different access methods in combination.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the personal music digital library must support a wide variety of user behaviors, from the most basic (e.g., browsing) to the most sophisticated (e.g., creating playlists).
a digital library of personal music should provide a variety of organization techniques, and that these techniques should be integrated in such a way that users may easily switch between them.
the organization of music collections is not a one-time event, but an on-going process.
